observations:
Torah #101 is a brief, tightly focused teaching with only two conceptual domains:

1. The GOOD domain: prayer-speech in all its forms (Tikkun Chatzot, hitbodedut, Tehillim, supplications, requests) united by the practice of 'פָּרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ' — expressing one's heart to God.

2. The EVIL domain: the yetzer hara and its warfare, including its inner expressions as weakness (chalishut) and confusions (bilbulim).

A possible candidate for a third package might be 'תְּשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה' (complete repentance), which appears once in line 6: 'שֶׁיּוֹצִיא אוֹתוֹ מֵחֹשֶׁךְ לְאוֹר וְיַחֲזִירֵהוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה בֶּאֱמֶת'. However, this is framed as the GOAL of prayer (an eitza relationship: prayer → teshuva), not as an independent thematic cluster. The Torah does not develop teshuva with bechina-language connections to other concepts — it appears only as the endpoint of successful prayer. It is therefore an eitza destination rather than a bechina cluster.

Similarly, 'הִתְקָרֵב לְהַשֵּׁם' (drawing close to God) appears as the goal-result of prayer — again an eitza destination, not an independent package.

The three closing scriptural verses (lines 9-11) are citations/support, not conceptual nodes with bechina connections.

Conclusion: The two packages (Prayer/Speech and Yetzer's Warfare) exhaust the Torah's conceptual structure. No independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts remains unaccounted for.
